messages:
ryan: FYI hit a hard limit while scaling the gpu-fleet in us-west-2 — several instances failed to attach to the NLB via the VPC endpoint. Seeing 'Target registration failed: TooManyTargets' errors in the autoscaler logs. Opening a support case now. :grimacing:

maria: ugh saw the same on the canary earlier, but it recovered after an hour. do we have current quota numbers for vpce-targets/target groups in that account?

sandeep: quick check — account-prod-2 has 350 targets per NLB/target-group default in us-west-2. our planned burst would have registered ~420 during rolling scale. that explains it.

olivia: can we short-circuit by routing some pods to a fallback model variant endpoint in another region while AWS processes the quota increase? cost implications?

ryan: yes fallback is doable but increases cross-region egress and adds ~18% cost for that batch. prefer to get quota bump. opening AWS case: Case# 1209876543. link: https://console.aws.amazon.com/support/cases#/case/?id=1209876543 :thumbsup:

infra-bot: deploy-checklist: noticed 12 failed registrations 2026-03-15T16:03Z -> autoscaler retried 3 times, then rolled back.

maria: logs from kube-proxy on the nodes show these lines:
```
2026-03-15T16:02:51Z ERROR target-registration: RegisterTargets failed: TooManyTargets
2026-03-15T16:03:12Z WARN healthcheck: target not healthy after attach
```

sandeep: I already drafted the quota request text for AWS: "Request increase for NLB/TargetGroup targets from 350 -> 600 in us-west-2 for account-prod-2 to support GPU scaling and burst deployments. Traffic pattern: short bursts during deployments and autoscaling, average 220 targets, 95th 460." want me to submit or should someone from infra billing attach cost justification?

olivia: pls include cost justification. add estimated delta: +$3k/mo for hitting higher target usage but we avoid service disruption and emergency region failover.

ryan: submitted the case with the justification and a note that we need expedited review. AWS auto-replied with a follow-up ticket id and asked for VPC/Account IDs. I've posted those in the case.

aws-support-bot: AWS Support: Case 1209876543 acknowledged. Estimated initial review within 4 business hours. If you need faster response reply with 'escalate'.

maria: in the meantime I'm going to throttle rollout: reduced parallelism from 20 -> 8 for this deployment and added delay_between_batches=60s. should reduce instantaneous targets to ~280.

ryan: good call. I'll also flip routing policy to prefer existing regional pools to avoid new registrations where possible. :eyes:

sandeep: after the quota increase request we should consider a long-term mitigation: cross-account target groups or smaller target group sharding to avoid hitting single-group max. filing an RFC ticket.

olivia: can you add the SLA/cost tradeoff table to the RFC? PMs will want numbers.

ryan: noted. I'll update the rollout runbook with temporary throttle steps and link the AWS case. last update here when case changes. thanks all. :v:
